nodes.label: ADR 0001: Adopt OKF v0.2 as the bundle format
ADR 0003: Path-based visibility with a link-closure lint
ADR 0005: An entity layer over the document graph
ADR 0006: The starter pack is not the product
ADR 0007: The engine ships as an npm package, published from the export
ADR 0008: Evals drive the production compiler through a bridge; judges are agents
ADR 0009: One ledger for turns, spans and payloads — not sessions
ADR 0010: A judgment is evidence only with a confidence interval, a human check, and a hash
ADR 0012: Direct adapters are canonical; a gateway is a fallback that fills only the keys that are absent
ADR 0014: Coding agents reach the framework through a skills suite shipped in the package, written by the Scribe from briefs
ADR 0015: Background work is a queue the tools write and a separate worker drains, not a tool that runs agents
ADR 0016: Production templates live in their own directory beside the starter pack, not as rewrites of it
ADR 0017: The engine is a library with plug points; the adopter supplies identity, credentials and storage
ADR 0018: Agent files are the source of truth; the registry is opt-in, explicit, versioned and loud
ADR 0019: "Multi-model" means orchestration parity, stated as a tested capability matrix
ADR 0020: Memory is keyed by a stored namespace and a supplied scope key, computed by a configured provider, saved at least once, and erased in one operation
ADR 0021: One Postgres connection holds every durable store; in-memory is the single-instance default; Redis is optional
ADR 0022: This repository becomes the public source of truth; private deployments consume the package
ADR 0023: Each provider accepts a configured endpoint and credential source, including Vertex AI, Bedrock and Azure OpenAI
ADR 0024: Google ADK stays the agent runtime, behind the framework's own turn runner; A2A is the wire, in both directions
ADR 0025: Built-in authenticators — per-caller tokens with a stable scope, JWT, a trusted gateway header; billing stays separate
ADR 0026: Governance on the policy plug point — daily budgets per caller and scope, one record per task, Prometheus metrics, ledger redaction
ADR 0027: A chat-completions turn that thinks but never answers is a named error
ADR 0028: A tool can require a human approval, per agent, through A2A input-required
ADR 0029: An agent holds Agent Skills the way a coding harness does: the index injected, one skill read on demand, scripts run only after approval
ADR 0030: A syndicate can be a graph: the `workflow:` block, on ADK's Workflow, is the third orchestration method
ADR 0031: An agent asks the person through `ask_user`, a long-running tool on the input-required path
ADR 0032: Any HTTP API with an OpenAPI spec becomes an agent's tools through `openapi:`, read-only by default
ADR 0033: Three ADK agent features as YAML keys, each placed where it means something: code_execution, context, mode
ADR 0034: Self-correction is on by default (ADK's reflect-and-retry plugins); url_context and examples join the agent surface
ADR 0035: Moonshot AI (Kimi) is a direct provider; its search stays off the model
ADR 0036: OpenAPI calls follow redirects one hop at a time, under the SSRF guard
ADR 0037: The hardening check runs on every storage path, judged by what could expose the tables
ADR 0038: A graceful stop fails readiness first, inside the grace budget
ADR 0039: A public deployment states its posture; turns and users have default caps
ADR 0040: Releases ship from a version tag, with npm provenance and an SBOM; CI is pinned and scanned
ADR 0041: Tool vendors get least privilege: OpenAPI auth cannot read framework secrets; MCP tools are allowlisted, gateable and bounded
ADR 0042: An append-only audit trail of who did what, from where
ADR 0043: A caller's trace context is linked, never adopted
ADR 0044: An agent may name a fallback model; a provider that keeps failing is skipped for a cooldown
ADR 0045: Own the runtime behind the seam: a native runtime beside ADK, built in stages, with ADK removed at 1.0
ADR 0046: Provider reasoning state rides on the content part it belongs before
ADR 0047: One provider-neutral reasoning key, mapped per provider by the compiler
ADR 0048: The engine owns its model message format, not @google/genai Content
ADR 0049: Claude requests follow the model generation
ADR 0050: The Responses adapters replay encrypted reasoning items and store nothing with the vendor
ADR 0051: Tools are the engine's own, with a delta-aware context, and reach ADK through one wrapper
ADR 0052: The engine types the stored event as it is, and gives sessions and memory interfaces of its own
ADR 0053: The caller of a contract adapter charges the turn and opens its llm.request span; on the ADK path that caller is the shim
ADR 0055: Claude moves onto the contract and the ADK path keeps its request: the older reasoning spelling rides as an ADK-only extension, and tool results keep ADK's JSON
ADR 0056: GptLlm and GrokLlm keep the Responses usage meaning and the server-side tool record on the ADK path
ADR 0057: The chat-completions adapters move onto the contract; their ADK shims keep the shape ADK saw and carry the older spelling
ADR 0058: The session stores implement both session interfaces, and a bridge gives a store that has one the other
ADR 0059: Memory and its tools are the engine's own: one service on both interfaces, recall through the tool context, and tools that write into the instruction
ADR 0061: JSON mode without a schema is a contract field, outputFormat: 'json'

attrs.description: Drafts one client follow-up message from the facts it is given, and nothing else.
Web researcher for anything that must be current or sourced.
Summarizes pasted text or up to five web pages.

Carries out a multi-step job described in plain language, such as reading and comparing several pages or drafting a document, and returns the finished result, ending with one line on anything it could not do.
Web search + source reading: verifies specific claims and establishes the documented record from wire services, primary sources, and diverse outlets.

Live X (Twitter) fact-gathering through the X API, pictures included: what is being claimed and by whom, how different camps frame the topic, what is disputed, and what the photos attached to posts say.
Maps the knowledge graph: has the Surveyor read prose for relations a parser cannot see, and the Registrar record them with their evidence.
Records ONE proposed relation through the wiki_relate gate (tools: wiki_graph, wiki_read, wiki_relate) and reports what the gate said.

Reads an area of the knowledge bundle and proposes typed relations a parser cannot derive (depends_on, constrains, supersedes, explains, alternative_to, mitigates, contradicts), each with the quotation supporting it and both node ids resolved against the graph.
Opens a status page, vendor documentation page or log link and reports what it says about the question.
Finds the relevant procedure, known issue or past postmortem in the team's runbook bundle.
Builds the strongest honest case FOR a claim or plan.
Builds the strongest honest case AGAINST a claim or plan.
Reviews one draft answer against the user's question.
Writes the answer to the user's question.
Answers programming questions: writes, explains, and debugs code in any language.
Solves math and calculation questions: arithmetic, algebra, calculus, geometry, probability.
Writes or revises one piece of outbound text from a brief.
Checks a draft against the brief and the policy, rule by rule.
Holds a deliverable (a file, a configuration, a command sequence) against the rules the skill it was made from states for it.
Finds facts for one research question with web search.
Writes the finished deliverable from research notes.
Compares an approved image spec (JSON payload) against a blind visual inventory (text).
The only agent with access to the library catalog, via MCP tools discovered at runtime: search_catalog, read_scroll, borrow_scroll, annotate_scroll.
Claude Sonnet, by Anthropic.
Gemini Flash Lite, by Google.
GPT-5 mini, by OpenAI.
Grok 4.7 (reasoning effort: medium), by xAI.
Kimi K3 (reasoning effort: low), by Moonshot AI; open weights.
Qwen 3.5 (9B), an open-weight model running locally via Ollama.
Use this subagent for real-time medical research: current treatment guidelines, drug information and interactions, what a test or procedure measures, typical recovery timelines, and recent findings.
Answers a request that is not an article.
Lists the claims a piece on this brief would have to get right.
Merges the Writer's draft and the Checker's list into the final draft.
Applies the person's decision to the draft and returns the published text.
Writes the draft from the Planner's brief.
Returns sourced notes on one research question: at most 20 dated claims, each with its quote, publisher and URL, plus disagreements and gaps.
Checks a draft brief against the research notes it was built from and returns PASS or FIX with one line per problem.
Writes the brief from the research notes it is given and returns only the brief.
Opens up to six URLs and returns quoted notes on the question: each claim with the exact sentence it rests on, the publisher, the page's own URL and its date.
Returns sourced research notes on one question: at most 20 dated claims, each with its quote, publisher, URL and how directly the page supports it, plus disagreements and gaps.
Finds candidate pages for one search brief and returns up to five, each as URL, publisher, date and one line on why it is worth reading.
What a term, endpoint, phase, design or statistic means, and how to read one.
A body of evidence across studies: what is known about an intervention, an exposure or a mechanism, including what is recent.
ONE object: this trial, this paper, this identifier.
Reviews whether a change does what its stated intent claims, and only that, and returns findings lines or "no findings".
Reviews a change for rollout, rollback, migration and observability, and returns findings lines or "no findings".
Reviews a change for security, data, privacy, cost and blast radius, and returns findings lines or "no findings".
Checks one draft against its brief and returns JSON: ok, and a list of violations, each with the rule broken, the offending quote, and the fix.
Writes one reader-facing document from a brief, audits it through the Auditor, and returns the document alone.
Keeper of the knowledge bundle: answers what the house knows via the Seeker, records what it learns via the Illuminator.
Authors or revises one knowledge-bundle document per request, writing through the validated wiki_save gate (tools: wiki_map, wiki_search, wiki_read, wiki_links, wiki_save).
Answers one question from the knowledge bundle using navigation tools (wiki_map, wiki_search, wiki_read, wiki_links, wiki_dive), returning the substance plus the bundle paths it came from.
Answers in the terse register: telegraphic, dense, zero filler — the analyst's briefing.
Answers in the stoic-mentor register: flowing, reflective, exact.
Answers in the structured-peer register: warm, scannable, encouraging, practical.
Looks up or changes this customer's own records through the tools your systems expose over MCP.
How-to, feature, setting, limit and error-message questions answered from the documentation bundle.
Hands the case to a person: complaints, legal or safety matters, exceptions, bug reports, requests for a person, and anything unclear.
Use this subagent to perform a web search for the latest news on a given topic.
Calls the company's systems through the operations their MCP server publishes and returns each call's operation, parameters and result verbatim.
Ask Crossref and OpenAlex whether a DOI has been retracted, withdrawn, or had an expression of concern issued.
What has cited a paper, most cited first, through OpenAlex.
Resolve ONE identifier to its record: an NCT number, a DOI, a PMID or a PMCID.
Search PEER-REVIEWED literature (PubMed and PubMed Central) through Europe PMC.
Search PREPRINT servers (bioRxiv, medRxiv and the rest of Europe PMC's preprint index).
Search the ClinicalTrials.gov registry.
How much has been published on a subject and the most cited of it, through OpenAlex.
Add a task to the user's own to-do list: something THEY need to do or remember.
Read one task or background job in full, including a finished job's result.
List the user's tasks and background jobs, one line each with id, status, and title.
Queue a background job: work that takes a while (reading several pages, a long draft, a comparison) and should not block the conversation.
Change a task: mark it done, cancel it, reopen it, or edit its title, notes, or due date.
Read web pages in full.
Repo dive: given a TASK, get an ordered reading plan through the bundle — orientation indexes first, then matched concepts, then graph-linked context, within a word budget.
Delegate a wiki edit to a gardener agent: author a new concept document or revise existing ones from an instruction.

Query the ENTITY graph: agents, syndicates, models, providers, tools, MCP servers, modules, tables, env vars, npm scripts and documents, joined by typed relations (uses_tool, uses_model, imports, reads_table, requires_env, documents, depends_on, constrains…).
Walk the knowledge graph from one document: what it links to and what links to it, out to a chosen depth.
Orient in the knowledge bundle: its purpose, directory map, document census, and graph health.
Ask the knowledge bundle a question in natural language.
Read one wiki document by bundle path (e.g.
Assert ONE typed relation the build cannot derive — a judgment read out of prose (depends_on, constrains, supersedes, explains, alternative_to, mitigates, contradicts).
Write one concept document into the bundle (create or revise).
Lexical search over the knowledge bundle (titles, tags, headings, paths, body).
Search X (Twitter) posts from the last 7 days through the X API and read the pictures.
